claim: The artifact is an ExteraGram Python plugin with metadata requiring app >=12.5.1 and SDK >=1.4.4.3; these are declared constraints, not runtime-verified compatibility.
recipe: Treat the app/SDK metadata as the author's requested compatibility floor; verify against the target client's loader and SDK before distribution.

claim: The plugin uses Android MediaCodecList to discover existing AV1 and HEVC decoder components; this repository does not bundle dav1d/libgav1 or another decoder implementation.
recipe: Check the target device's registered MediaCodec inventory; installing this plugin alone does not add an AV1 codec.

claim: On API 29+ decoder software classification uses isSoftwareOnly() or the negation of isHardwareAccelerated(); below API 29 it falls back to codec-name heuristics.
recipe: When reusing the scan, account for both Android's classification fields and the older name-based fallback; do not assume names are authoritative on every vendor build.

claim: The system decoder scan records upper supported width and height bounds where available; failure to read video capabilities leaves the codec recorded with zero bounds.
recipe: Keep capability-query failure separate from codec discovery failure when presenting supported decoder limits.

claim: Discovered software decoders are sorted with codec names containing dav1d first.
api: sw.sort(key=lambda d: 0 if DAV1D_MARK in d[0].lower() else 1)
recipe: Use decoder-name ordering only as a preference; the scan does not benchmark performance on the current device.

claim: AV1 support is overridden only when Telegram's original supportsHardwareDecoder result is false, the codec string is av1/av01, software AV1 exists, the plugin is enabled, and software AV1 has not failed.
recipe: Gate capability overrides on actual codec availability and an explicit enabled setting, and retain the original result for all other formats.

claim: In default fallback mode, AV1 quality URIs are removed when any non-AV1 URI exists; in always mode they remain alongside alternatives unless filtered by the resolution cap.
recipe: Model fallback as a quality-list policy and separately account for resolution filtering; the latter still applies in both modes.

claim: The AV1 cap compares min(width,height) to the selected threshold, so it constrains the shorter image dimension rather than specifically the vertical height.
recipe: When documenting the cap, describe it using its implemented min-dimension rule rather than assuming a portrait-oriented height field.

claim: If the quality filter would otherwise remove every URI, it preserves one dropped AV1 URI with the smallest pixel area; empty quality groups are then removed.
api: smallest = min(drop, key=lambda u: u.width * u.height)
recipe: Preserve a lowest-cost candidate when applying quality filters so a video with no in-cap variant does not become unplayable solely from filtering.

claim: MediaCodecUtil decoder ordering is activated for AV1 only after the AV1 support override was used; HEVC ordering requires the separate force_sw_hevc setting.
recipe: Keep codec-list reordering tied to the format whose capability path opted into software decode; expose other codecs behind a distinct opt-in.

claim: When reordering is active, software decoder candidates rank before hardware; dav1d ranks first only when prefer_dav1d is enabled, and hardware entries remain available at the end.
recipe: Preserve lower-priority decoders in the reordered list so renderer fallback can reach them.

claim: The plugin sets the private DefaultRenderersFactory field enableDecoderFallback to true when can_override() permits software AV1 (before override_used is required) or when software HEVC is available and opted in.
recipe: Check the plugin conditions separately from actual decoder selection: this fallback field can be enabled before an AV1 eligibility override has occurred.

claim: A player error disables further AV1 capability override until plugin/app reload only when software override was previously used and the error/cause text contains av1 or av01.
recipe: Use a fail-closed state after decoder errors, while recognizing that substring classification can misidentify error cause.

claim: Hooks compare a per-instance token stored on shared sys before callbacks run; unload clears the current token, cancels the diagnostic timer, and unhooks saved callbacks.
recipe: Use an instance-generation guard so stale callbacks become no-ops after reload, and retain unhook handles for normal unload cleanup.

claim: The plugin resolves application classes with ApplicationLoader.applicationContext.getClassLoader(); ExoPlayer lookup tries the com.google.android.exoplayer2 namespace before androidx.media3.exoplayer.
recipe: Resolve hook targets with the target app's class loader and handle both legacy ExoPlayer and Media3 package names explicitly.

claim: The plugin has no explicit Android API-level minimum check: startup scans actual system codecs and skips hook installation only when neither software AV1 nor software HEVC is present; API 29 changes codec classification, not an enforced minimum.
recipe: Treat codec inventory as device-specific; do not infer Android 10 compatibility from the API 29 classification branch.

claim: Diagnostics POST JSON to https://stxlvn.tech/av1log with 15-second connect and read timeouts; scheduled delivery is gated by send_logs and coalesces reasons on a daemon timer, while the manual log action starts a worker and calls send directly.
recipe: Audit manual and automatic upload paths separately; a preference check on scheduled sends does not imply that explicit manual send is disabled.

claim: Regular diagnostics redact tg://, storage/data paths, file://, and HTTP(S) URL fragments from event strings before buffering them.
recipe: Describe redaction narrowly by its implemented patterns; do not claim that arbitrary filenames or all sensitive text are removed.

claim: The separate manual SDK dump collects module file paths, version attributes, and up to 180 KiB of inspect.getsource per module; it does not pass these values through the regular event redaction function.
recipe: Review the exact module/source payload and obtain informed opt-in before using SDK introspection uploads; ordinary log redaction does not cover this path.

claim: The settings UI exposes AV1 enable, fallback/always mode, five resolution limits, dav1d preference, unsupported flag reset, opt-in software HEVC, and a hidden diagnostics page toggled by long-press.
api: create_settings() -> List[Any]; Switch; Selector; Text; Header; Divider
recipe: Use long-press callbacks for secondary diagnostics controls only when the plugin settings UI supports the same callback contract.

claim: The complete captured upstream tree has three blobs (.gitignore, README.md, av1_sw_decoder.plugin); the content manifest captures README and plugin only. The tree has no visible build scripts, tests, CI workflow, or license file, and GitHub repository metadata declares no license.
recipe: Distinguish upstream tree inventory from the two-file content manifest; do not infer package/release reproducibility or license.

claim: README states Android 10+ is required and warns high-resolution software decoding may be slow on weak CPUs; these are documentation claims without device measurements in this repository.
recipe: Use the cap to reduce candidate resolution when needed, but measure playback on the specific device before promising performance.

claim: README instructs users to download the plugin from Releases, send it to Saved Messages in exteraGram, and tap the file; the repository snapshot does not include a release artifact.
recipe: Treat this as the documented installation route only; inspect a pinned release separately when evaluating the distributed artifact.

claim: At startup the plugin becomes idle without hooks only if neither software AV1 nor software HEVC is discovered; missing Telegram VideoPlayer is separately recorded and stops installation.
recipe: Expose scan results and the first missing hook target separately in diagnostics to distinguish device capability from client-version mismatch.

claim: The plugin searches legacy ExoPlayer then AndroidX Media3 package names, but depends on reflective method names and a private renderer field that are not validated by the captured repository against any client build.
recipe: Pin and inspect target client internals before porting reflective hooks; names and fields are version-sensitive seams.

claim: The plugin warning text says a system software AV1 decoder exists starting with Android 10, but the plugin detects the codec inventory dynamically and this repository does not establish that every Android 10 device provides one.
recipe: Treat the Android 10 statement as UI copy; confirm MediaCodecList on the target device.

claim: The settings UI describes dav1d as usually faster than libgav1, while the implementation only ranks codec names and contains no benchmark; the speed comparison is an unverified UI claim.
recipe: Treat decoder preference as ordering behavior, not a performance guarantee; benchmark on the target hardware before making throughput claims.

claim: This repository provides an ExteraGram plugin integration around existing Android codec components, not a reusable AV1 decoder library or a plugin SDK; its only implementation file imports plugin APIs and Java/Android classes.
api: BasePlugin, MethodHook, MediaCodecList, Java reflection hooks
recipe: Use this source as a plugin integration example, not as a decoder implementation or SDK contract; the ExteraGram SDK implementation is outside the captured repository.
